title: Brass bands at Australian conventions
summary: Bull explains how brass bands began at Australian jazz conventions, older musicians' scorn, and the lack of friendly societies.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: When did these brass bands start really? About three or four years ago I think was the first one at the convention. Of course you have all the old Aiden Monspras and all the old Lou Waters type musicians go, what's all this rubbish, what's this garbage, that's not jazz. Anyway, they started off having one then and they've had one every convention since then but it's always been a sort of very disorganized thing. Last year was the first time we ever got an organization.

But they don't play otherwise, they don't play for funerals or anything. No sir. Do they have friendly societies in Australia, what they call friendly societies in England? Very rarely, very rarely. It's not a very well organized country like here where everybody is organization minded, huh?
No, they don't go very much for that sort of thing. You have Masonic lodges.
